title: Doors — Fwd Cargo Door Latching — Borescope Survey of the Latch Pin Housings
abstract: A borescope survey of the eight forward cargo door latch pin housings, giving operators a way of finding pin scoring before the bushings are changed and of deciding whether the pins themselves have to be replaced.

sections.planning_reason: Teardown of returned latch housings showed that dry running had scored the pins as well as the bushings in about a third of cases. An operator that changes only the bushings on a scored pin gets a second failure within a few thousand cycles. Because the pin is not visible without a borescope, operators had no way of making that decision before opening the housing. This survey is issued so that the material for the bushing change can be ordered with the right pin content.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives a borescope survey of the eight latch pin housings of the forward cargo door with the door in the open position and the latch mechanism driven to the unlocked stop. It records the condition of each pin and of each bushing bore against a photographic standard. The standard is the greased bronze bushing installation: an acceptable bore carries an even film of grease, and any dry, matt or discoloured area inside the bore is classified as contamination or as grease starvation and counts against the acceptance limit. The aircraft configuration is not changed by this Service Bulletin.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the forward cargo door and set the maintenance stay. Isolate the door actuation system. Drive the latch mechanism to the unlocked stop by hand and lock it there. Get access to each of the eight latch pin housings through the inspection openings in zones 891 and 893. Do a borescope survey of each pin and of each bushing bore. Compare each finding with the photographic standard in the accomplishment instructions and record the classification. Where a pin is classified beyond the acceptance limit, order the pin content with the bushing kit. Where the doubler assembly D5230134342244 shows fretting at the housing boss, report the finding to Aeralis. Restore the latch mechanism, remove the maintenance stay and do the door operational test.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00360, that is the population that is still at the greased bronze bushing standard. There is no pre-modification or post-modification condition on this survey: it is equally valid on an aircraft that has already had the bushings changed, as a condition record.
sections.material_note: No kit. A borescope with a 4 mm probe and a 90 degree side view is required and is not supplied. The photographic acceptance standard is issued as an appendix to this Service Bulletin and is also available through the operator portal.

type_data.compliance_time: Before ordering the material for Service Bulletin MRD-52-1024, at the operator's convenience.

tooling: Borescope, 4 mm probe, 90 degree side view

title: Doors — Fwd Cargo Door Latching — Borescope Survey of the Latch Pin Housings

issue.reason: Second set of acceptance criteria added for the dry self-lubricating liner and the claim that the survey is valid on any bushing standard withdrawn.

abstract: A borescope survey of the eight forward cargo door latch pin housings against two acceptance standards, one for the greased bronze bushing and one for the dry self-lubricating liner, so that pin scoring is found before the bushings are changed.

sections.planning_reason: Teardown of returned latch housings showed that dry running had scored the pins as well as the bushings in about a third of cases. An operator that changes only the bushings on a scored pin gets a second failure within a few thousand cycles. Because the pin is not visible without a borescope, operators had no way of making that decision before opening the housing. This survey is issued so that the material for the bushing change can be ordered with the right pin content.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin gives a borescope survey of the eight latch pin housings of the forward cargo door with the door in the open position and the latch mechanism driven to the unlocked stop. It records the condition of each pin and of each bushing bore against a photographic standard. Two standards are now published. Standard 1 is the greased bronze bushing installation, where an acceptable bore carries an even film of grease and a dry or matt area counts as grease starvation. Standard 2 is the self-lubricating liner installation of MOD-160915, where the bore is dry by design and develops a thin even transfer film in the first few hundred cycles; that film is evidence of correct running and must not be classified as contamination. Read the correct standard for the bushing fitted. The aircraft configuration is not changed by this Service Bulletin.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the forward cargo door and set the maintenance stay. Isolate the door actuation system. Drive the latch mechanism to the unlocked stop by hand and lock it there. Establish which bushing standard is installed from the aircraft configuration record before the first image is taken. Get access to each of the eight latch pin housings through the inspection openings in zones 891 and 893. Do a borescope survey of each pin and of each bushing bore. Compare each finding with the photographic standard for the bushing fitted and record the classification together with the standard used. Where a pin is classified beyond the acceptance limit, order the pin content with the bushing kit. Where the doubler assembly D5230134342244 shows fretting at the housing boss, report the finding to Aeralis. Restore the latch mechanism, remove the maintenance stay and do the door operational test.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to MRD-42K1 and MRD-46K1 aircraft from MSN M00001 through M00360. On aircraft at the greased bronze bushing standard, use acceptance standard 1. On aircraft that have embodied MOD-160915, use acceptance standard 2; a survey done against standard 1 on a self-lubricating liner is not valid and must be repeated, because the dry transfer film that a serviceable liner develops is classified as contamination by standard 1 and rejects an installation that is in fact correct.
sections.material_note: No kit. A borescope with a 4 mm probe and a 90 degree side view is required and is not supplied. Both photographic acceptance standards are issued as appendices to this Service Bulletin and are also available through the operator portal. The appendix for the self-lubricating liner is issued with this revision and carries its own image set; the two appendices must not be used together on one housing.

type_data.compliance_time: Before ordering the material for Service Bulletin MRD-52-1024, at the operator's convenience. On an aircraft already at the MOD-160915 standard, before the next latch housing condition record is raised.

tooling: Borescope, 4 mm probe, 90 degree side view

revision_history.reason: Acceptance standard 2 added for the self-lubricating liner
